name: Gianni Agnelli
role: Italian industrialist, Fiat chairman (1966–1996) and senator for life (1991–2003)
summary: Agnelli advocated open markets, European monetary and political integration, and Atlantic cooperation. He favored reforming costly welfare arrangements while supporting international development assistance and managed immigration; his labor relations combined negotiated cooperation with efforts to curb union power at Fiat.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: He advocates fiscal consolidation but later praises temporary countercyclical budget flexibility after September 11.

capital-controls.rationale: He promotes global liberalization of goods, services and capital.

class-collaboration.rationale: His producer pact proposes labor-capital cooperation against unproductive rents.

collective-bargaining.rationale: He signed the 1975 national wage-indexation agreement and defended restoring order to collective bargaining.

common-currency.rationale: He strongly advocates implementing the euro on schedule.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: He calls for welfare reform because excessive social spending undermines employment and investment; dependency is not his stated argument.

decide-locally.rationale: In 1992 he judged decentralisation of the ministries advisable to meet local needs, but only after a careful look because local bureaucracies are often less efficient than central ones.

defeat-communism.rationale: He opposes Soviet-bloc domination while explicitly pursuing peaceful East-West coexistence and commerce.

delink-world-market.rationale: He favors participation in global markets rather than isolation.

democracy-best.rationale: He explicitly affirms the superiority of democratic government.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: He said free elections, pluralism and parliamentary debate are not enough for a mature democracy, which also needs a legal and institutional culture and a strong civil society.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: He rejects closing Europe to outside commerce.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He praises the Atlantic integration that brought Italy into NATO.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: He defends Maastricht constraints as supports for European monetary integration.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: He said that in an open integrated Europe, mergers of Italian state firms with foreign ones can no longer be judged by old national reservations.

free-trade.rationale: He explicitly advocates worldwide trade liberalization as a source of prosperity.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: He said each great culture will find its own answer to modernity, not necessarily in tune with Western values, while still urging legal culture and democracy for Russia.

local-essentials-public.rationale: In 1997 he asked that small public firms spread across local services be returned to the market and managed by private owners free of political appointees; he did not speak to hospitals.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He argued that state-run sectors answer to power-sharing rather than market competition and so lose efficiency and quality, and that politically driven state investment in the South failed on economics; he said this was not an ideological stance.

nation-first.rationale: He says national protection requires international cooperation and continued integration.

open-borders.rationale: He explicitly rejects indiscriminate border opening as simplistic.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He calls for Europe to become a stronger unified political actor.

proportional-representation.rationale: He said the partly majoritarian system had not given stable government and suggested that a fully majoritarian electoral reform could be a useful premise for resolving the country's problems.

public-ownership.rationale: He urged that the moment had come to carry out privatisations in short order, said the state shareholder no longer had the means to run its holdings, and called for returning public industrial and service firms, national and local, to the market.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He favors managing migration and investing in reception and integration, opposing sealed borders.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: He demands rich-country market access for poorer exporters and health exceptions to patents.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: He urges wealthy governments to increase resources for development infrastructure and education.

social-market-economy.rationale: He called for a market economy built on rules and controls that prevent arbitrariness, for a welfare state reorganised but not abolished, and against state-run enterprise.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He criticised large state investments in the South made without regard to economic viability (Alfasud, chemicals, steel) and said funds could no longer be used by bureaucratic, assistance-minded methods.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He welcomes Italy’s Western alignment and rejects joining the Soviet bloc.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The record points both ways: in 1991 he wanted Japanese cars kept out of European markets until 1998-99, but in 1994 and 1999 he welcomed giving up protections in the single market and called protectionist autarky a brake. The two passes found statements pulling both ways, so 0.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He endorses replacing conquest and domination with international cooperation.

unions-good.rationale: He negotiated major union agreements but subsequently backed reducing union influence within Fiat.

notes:
No inferred answers. Reviewed all statement themes and remaining nulls. Social, ecological and technological positions are not inferred from his occupation, family, private life or business products. The 1997 conference contains many speakers: only Agnelli’s own intervention between its introduction and the moderator’s thanks is used. Welfare retrenchment is qualified because he criticized costs, not explicitly personal dependency. Opposition to communist bloc rule is distinguished from hostility to all coexistence with communist states. Full texts downloaded and searched where direct retrieval succeeded; the Senate PDF was read through the web tool after direct download was blocked.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 10 answers taken from it, 16 agreed, 1 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass (does not copy the first audit); built mostly from his own speeches in Radio Radicale recordings (automatic transcripts, only his own segment used, so medium confidence at most), L'Unità reports of his remarks (1991, 1998, 1999) and Treccani. Themes searched: economy, government, world, globalism, means. Society, liberty, culture, ecology and technology are almost silent in his public record; Italian Senate texts on senato.it were not reachable and the Sala Zuccari lecture of 21 January 2002 has no transcript on Radio Radicale. His 1991 remarks and 1999 and 1997 speeches point both ways on protection and the welfare state, so those answers are 0 at low. Fiat's corporate acts (the 1976 Libya deal, the 1980 strike) are not used for answers except where he himself spoke to them.
